name: xmp
desc: Command-line player for module music formats (MOD, S3M, IT, etc)
why: Plays tracker module formats like MOD and S3M, a window into the old demoscene music world that most developers never touch.

brief.what_it_is: xmp, the Extended Module Player, is a portable command-line player for tracker music files. You give it a module file such as an Impulse Tracker .it or a Protracker .mod and it renders the song to audio. The homepage says it plays many mainstream and obscure formats, including Protracker MOD, Scream Tracker 3 S3M, Fast Tracker II XM and Impulse Tracker IT. Its terminal screen shows the module name, type, pattern and channel counts, duration, and a live position readout, and single keypresses move between patterns and songs, mute channels, and show instrument and sample lists. The player is a front end to libxmp, a separate library that renders module audio as linear PCM.
brief.why_it_exists: The project is framed as preservation and playback of tracker music: the homepage calls the Amiga and PC trackers of the demoscene and related formats 'classic, rare or otherwise interesting' and lists archives such as Modland and Aminet. The author also wants libxmp to be reusable by other programs, for example players, information extractors, module-to-mp3 renderers and game music.
brief.how_it_works: Since release 4.0 the project is split into libxmp, a library that loads a module and renders it to PCM at a rate and format the caller chooses, and xmp, the player application built on it. The homepage says xmp can read compressed modules using built-in depackers for formats such as zip, gzip, xz and LHA, or external helpers (unmo3 for MO3, unrar for RAR). In archives only the first module is played. The README says xmp -L lists supported formats.

commands_seen.context: Homepage example: plays one Impulse Tracker module file and prints its header info and a live playback status line, with 'Press h for help'.
From the GitHub README: lists the available command-line options.
From the GitHub README: lists the supported module formats.

brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install: the homepage describes xmp as the player that sits on top of libxmp, so the player release needs libxmp 4.4.0 or newer and recommends 4.7.0 or newer. The brew formula is named xmp and installs an xmp executable. Playback uses the audio system the homepage example shows (ALSA on Linux). Interactive mode can be turned off with --nocmd. No accounts, API keys or special hardware are mentioned. I did not check the Homebrew formula itself, so I cannot confirm its exact dependencies.
brief.standout: It handles a very wide range of formats, including obscure Amiga, Atari, Acorn and game-specific ones, with a long supported-formats list and dozens of packer and depacker variants. Its interactive controls (pattern skip, song skip, per-channel mute, instrument and sample dumps) work like a tracker's own view of a song, which is unusual for a command-line tool.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as the pages show. The homepage gives xmp 4.3.1 released July 30 2026 and libxmp 4.7.4 released October 10 2026, and the README copyright reads 1996-2026. I could not see a last-commit date on the GitHub page, so recent activity is inferred from those release dates.
brief.caveats: The homepage says a few incomplete formats such as DTT and DMF were disabled in recent releases, and that Flextrax effects are not supported. MO3 and RAR need external helper programs. The player is GPL v2 or later, while the libxmp 'lite' build is MIT-licensed and covers only MOD, S3M, XM and IT. The homepage has a stray fragment ('below)') and a mismatch with the README on format count ('many' versus 'over 90'). The brew description and the scout notes are the Homebrew formula's own text. The homepage example and the README use different interactive key lists, so check the README for the current keys.
quotes: The Extended Module Player, or xmp, is a portable command-line module player.
Xmp is able to play compressed modules using external helpers or built-in depackers.
Run xmp --help for a list of available options, or xmp -L to list the supported module formats.
Interactive mode can be disabled using the --nocmd command line option.

judge.reason: A little-known player that exposes tracker music as patterns, channels, instruments, and samples—a hands-on doorway into demoscene composition and its many surviving formats.

entry.title: xmp
entry.tldr: A terminal player for tracker music files like MOD, S3M, XM and IT, the sample-and-pattern formats of the demoscene, with per-channel muting.
entry.deeper_look:
xmp, the Extended Module Player, plays tracker modules: small files that hold a song as patterns of notes plus the samples or instruments used to play them. Give it a Protracker .mod, a Scream Tracker .s3m, a Fast Tracker II .xm or an Impulse Tracker .it, and it renders the song to audio. The homepage says it handles many mainstream and obscure formats, including Amiga, Atari and Acorn ones.

The terminal screen shows the module name, type, pattern and channel counts, duration and a live position readout. Single keypresses skip between patterns and songs, mute individual channels, and show instrument and sample lists. That makes it behave a bit like a tracker's own view of a song, so you can solo the bassline or see what a sample was called.

Since release 4.0 the project is split in two. libxmp is a library that loads a module and renders it to linear PCM at a rate and format the caller picks. xmp is the player built on top of it. The author wants the library reused elsewhere, for example in players, information extractors, module-to-mp3 renderers and game music. The homepage frames the whole thing as preservation of music that the demoscene trackers produced, and points to archives such as Modland and Aminet for files to play.

xmp can also read compressed modules, with built-in depackers for formats such as zip, gzip, xz and LHA. In an archive it plays only the first module.
entry.install:
brew install xmp
# pulls in libxmp; no accounts or special hardware needed. You need a module file to play, e.g. from Modland or Aminet.

try_this.what_happens: Lists every module format this build can play.
Plays the homepage's example Impulse Tracker module, printing its header info and a live status line. Press h for help.
Lists the command-line options, including --nocmd to turn off interactive mode.

entry.whats_unique: It covers a very wide range of obscure tracker formats and packers. Its interactive controls (pattern skip, channel mute, instrument and sample dumps) are unusual for a command-line player.
entry.caveats: A few incomplete formats such as DTT and DMF were disabled in recent releases, MO3 and RAR need external helpers, and the homepage and README list different interactive keys, so check the README.
